title: Design a Rare-event Detection System
interviewAnswer: Clarify the cost of false negatives/positives, label delay, class imbalance and response-time requirement. Optimize the operating threshold around business risk and monitor drift plus delayed ground truth.
why: Rare-event system design is a classic interview problem because metrics, latency, class imbalance and feedback delay all matter.
intuition: Score each event quickly, optimize for the cost of false negatives/positives, and combine model predictions with rules/manual review where necessary.
deepDive: Define decision latency and fraud label delay. Build point-in-time features from transaction/user/device history. Train with representative historical splits and class-aware loss/sampling. Calibrate scores and select thresholds from financial/review-capacity costs. Online path computes/fetches low-latency features, scores and triggers allow/review/block decisions. Labels arrive later from chargebacks/manual review, enabling monitoring/retraining.
workedExample: A threshold sends top-risk 0.5% transactions to review while an extreme-risk threshold blocks automatically; evaluate captured fraud value and customer false declines, not accuracy.
commonMistakes: Using future chargeback information in training features.
followUps: What if model service is down?
production: Use low-latency feature stores/caches, rules fallback, shadow/canary rollout, drift/adversarial monitoring and human-review feedback loops.
